claim: Consistency check: stage 1 takes no more heat than the absorber keeps after top and edge losses (10.5 of 15.1 MJ/m2 absorbed)
law: First law at the absorber node; a check of the solver's integration, not an independent result (independent review)

claim: Consistency check: stage 2 takes in no more than the heat crossing gap 1 (9.1 of 9.2 MJ/m2)
law: First law: heat into stage 2 is the latent, conducted, radiated and rib heat crossing gap 1, less edge loss (like quantities)

claim: Gained output ratio 1.29 quasi-steady (1.22 after warm-up) is below the ideal limit for four stages
law: Ideal multi-effect still: GOR <= N x tau x alpha (every effect reuses all the heat, no losses)

claim: Daily distillate 10.3 L/m2 (10.9 L quasi-steady) on a 5.5 kWh/m2 day (an upper-bound screen only)
law: Multi-effect upper bound: N stages x single-stage evaporation limit at tau alpha (limits.evaporation_kg_per_m2_day)

claim: Latent flux across a 6 mm gap with 5 K across it is about 362 W/m2 at a 60 C brine-wet wick face (water activity 0.972)
law: Fick diffusion with the Stefan flow correction, independent property fits; cf. Chiavazzo et al. 2018

claim: Conduction across the still 6 mm gap is about 23 W/m2 at 5 K (Nu = 1, heated from above)
law: Fourier conduction, k air 0.028 W/mK; stable stratification (Incropera, ch. 9)

claim: Painted fins and underside reject the peak 286 W/m2 at 25 K above ambient (effective 11.5 W/m2K per m2 of aperture)
law: Downward-facing natural plus laminar forced convection over the finned area, radiation at emissivity 0.90 (Incropera)
closed_by: SSK-DEC-001 D-07 (painted underside and fins; CAL v0.8)

claim: Dry stagnation holds the absorber near 138 C (142 C in calm air) at 1,000 W/m2 and 35 C
law: Absorbed flux = (U top + U down) x rise; U top about 5.5 W/m2K, four dry gaps and the fins in series below
check: claimed 103 K above ambient, estimate 90.7 K above ambient (ratio 1.14)

claim: 0.5 mm plates sag about 0.5 mm between ribs at 194 mm pitch, under one sixth of the 6 mm gap
law: Simply supported strip, w = 5 q L^4 / 384 E I, aluminium E 69 GPa, 22.6 N/m2

claim: A plate grows about 1.4 mm across 1 m at a 60 K rise, inside the 2 mm clearance each side
law: Linear expansion, aluminium 23e-6 /K

claim: Stage 3 side rails survive calm-air dry stagnation (107 C) with at least 10 K margin
law: Long-term service temperature in air: PPS 218 C (Mitsubishi Chemical Tecatron 1000 PPS); printed PC softens at 113 C (ISO 75, 0.45 MPa)

claim: Stage 1 and 2 PPS rails and silicone ribs survive 142 C calm-air stagnation
law: PPS long-term service 218 C (datasheet); silicone rubber cord rated about 200 C (supplier class)

claim: The inner twin-wall glazing sheet stays below its service limit at calm-air stagnation (113 C)
law: Twin-wall polycarbonate service temperature -40 to 120 C (Multicraft TW6C624 data)
closed_by: Kept with the stagnation cover and shade rule as the barrier, the rule on the panel label (SSK-DEC-001 D-05, decided by Amish 2026-10-25)

claim: M10 pivot bolt bearing on 12 mm plywood is about 1.4 MPa with the wet panel and 17 m/s wind
law: Embedment strength of plywood f_h = 0.11 (1 - 0.01 d) rho_k (EN 1995-1-1, eq. 8.20), rho_k 500 kg/m3

claim: A 45 x 45 mm timber prop, 1.0 m pinned, does not buckle under the panel and wind load (about 0.4 kN)
law: Euler buckling, softwood E 8 GPa

claim: Anchored (four stakes or 40 kg of ballast, a hold point), the panel and stand do not tip below 17 m/s of wind (PR-013); unanchored it tips at 16.5 m/s
law: Moment balance about the front end of the ground frame: normal force 0.5 rho v^2 Cf A (Cf 1.2) at the panel centre against the wet weight plus 40 kg of ballast at the rear of the ground rails
closed_by: SSK-DEC-001 D-09 (decided by Amish 2026-10-25); stake pull-out in soft or sandy ground to check at TRL 5

claim: A 1 mm wick carries the 1.44 kg/h per metre of width that stage 1 needs at noon if its permeability is 3.0e-11 m2 or more
law: Darcy flow, gravity along 20 deg plus 4 kPa capillary pressure (SSK-CAL-001 section 6)
check: Needed 3.0e-11 m2; permeability of the shortlisted fabrics not yet measured (wicking-rise test, SSK-DEC-001)

claim: The gravity feed needs no pump: the trough rim is at most 1.00 m above the ground at 35 deg
law: Hydrostatic head from a user-filled container at most 1.5 m (R5)

claim: Brine leaves at 66.7 g/L from 40 g/L feed at a feed ratio of 2.5, so salt stays in solution
law: Salt mass balance; NaCl saturation about 317 g/L of solution at 25 to 80 C (CRC Handbook)

claim: Dissolved salt does not evaporate with the vapour, so distillate salinity comes only from liquid carryover
law: Raoult's law; NaCl is non-volatile at still temperatures
check: The 8.2 mL/day of SSK-CAL-001 section 7 is an allowance for 50 mg/L, not a computed carryover (rows S29, PR-003); volatile organics can carry over (PRC safety)

claim: Bare 3003 or 1050 aluminium plate undersides survive contact with hot (60 to 80 C) brine-wet wicks for years
law: 3000 and 5000 series aluminium resists seawater to 125 C; crevice corrosion under gaskets is the main concern (Kappes 2017); 1050 resists better than 3003 (Dumitrascu et al. 2016)
check: The wick under its clips is a crevice in 58 to 67 g/L brine; no crevice rate at 60 to 80 C found; a perforation would let brine reach the distillate face
closed_by: Corrosion coupon test in the TRL 4 plan, 1050 preferred over 3003; 5052 plates if the coupons show crevice attack (SSK-DEC-001 D-04, decided by Amish 2026-10-25)

claim: The fluoropolymer coating on the condensing faces is food-contact safe in hot salty distillate and tolerates 150 C dry
law: PTFE and PFA are stable well above 150 C; drinking-water contact needs an NSF/ANSI/CAN 61 or equivalent certificate
check: Coating class chosen, certified product not yet seen (SSK-DEC-001, to confirm item 8)

claim: Distillate is a raw product and is not claimed safe to drink without testing and disinfection
law: WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality, 4th ed. with first and second addenda (2022)
check: Stages run at 58 to 80 C, below pasteurization certainty; brine carryover can carry microbes; test (conductivity, E. coli) and disinfect (PRC safety)

claim: Long-term drinking of distillate needs remineralization; low dissolved solids are not a health target
law: WHO, Nutrients in Drinking Water (2005), on demineralized and desalinated water; WHO TDS fact sheet: no health-based value
check: 50 mg/L is used as a carryover check only (PRS PR-003)

claim: The wick fabric tolerates 150 C dry without losing its wicking, and conducts like the k 0.45 W/mK the CAL assumes
law: Polyester nonwovens soften well below their 250 C melt; glass-fibre fabric is stable far above 150 C; cellulose (cotton, viscose) degrades with time at 140 C
check: Fabric chosen by the wicking-rise test between a polyester-type nonwoven and a glass-fibre fabric (SSK-DEC-001, 2026-10-02); the CAL's k and dry mass are cotton or viscose values

claim: The design-day integration is resolved in time: halving the 15 min step moves the daily yield by under 1 %
law: Quasi-steady fsolve over a 10 h sine day (SSK-CAL-001 section 1); noon solution converged: True

claim: 10.3 L/m2/day is two to three times a single-basin still (3 to 5 L/m2/day)
law: Basin still 3 to 5 L/m2/day (SSK-PRB-001) times a gained-output gain of 2 to 3

claim: Vapour lost through the low-end tongue openings is about 25 mL/day (0.2 % of the yield)
law: Fick diffusion through the openings, 4 gaps, 60 C inside, 30 C at 60 % RH outside

claim: Brine does not drip from the wick onto the condensing face below, and condensate drops do not bridge the 6 mm gap to the wick
law: Capillary retention in an unsaturated wick; sessile drops on a 20 deg face slide at a few mm (capillary length 2.7 mm), below the 6 mm gap
check: A wick fed past its capacity or a hydrophobic (fluoropolymer) face holding pinned drops could carry brine across; per-stage conductivity at TRL 4 decides

claim: The 5052 aluminium wick clips survive in hot brine and do not attack the aluminium plates
law: Galvanic series in seawater: stainless steel is about 0.5 V nobler than aluminium, so the 304 clips first chosen drove aluminium corrosion; 5052 is a marine alloy within the same aluminium group as 1050 and 3003, so the couple is negligible
check: The clips touch bare plate in 58 to 67 g/L brine at 60 to 80 C. Fixed by D-08 (a), decided by Amish 2026-10-25: clips bent from 5052-H32 strip 0.4 x 8 mm, same shape; the crevice under the clip stays with S21 and the TRL 4 coupon test

claim: Carbonate and sulphate scale on the wicks stays within weekly rinsing
law: Seawater concentrated 1.7 times at 60 to 80 C exceeds calcium carbonate saturation; calcium sulphate stays below saturation at that factor
check: Scale rate not computed; the weekly rinse (PR-010) and a vinegar soak are the controls; the wicking-rise test should be repeated on a scaled wick

claim: Adhesives, glazing tape and sealant survive their stagnation temperatures
law: High-temperature silicone adhesives and sealants are commonly rated about 200 to 260 C; the fins sit at about 64 C, the tape under the glazing edge near the inner sheet (113 C calm)
check: Products not yet named; check each datasheet when buying (SSK-DEC-001, to confirm item 6)

claim: The glazing passes about 0.80 of the sun (solar-weighted, with incidence and dust losses)
law: The 80 % of the source is a light transmission; solar-weighted values with incidence-angle loss and soiling are likely 0.72 to 0.78 (independent review)
check: At 0.75 the design day gives 10.1 L quasi-steady (CAL sensitivity), so PR-001 is met only near 0.80; measure the sheet at TRL 4

claim: Brine lowers the wick's vapour pressure (water activity 0.972 at the mean wick salinity of 47 g/L), now in the CAL
law: Raoult's law with an osmotic coefficient of 0.93 for NaCl (CAL v0.8, added after the independent review)

claim: Option B makes about 3.8 L/m2/day at an assumed (not computed) 45 % daily efficiency on the 5.5 kWh/m2 day
law: Single-effect limit: evaporation <= tau alpha x sun / h_fg (limits.evaporation_kg_per_m2_day)

claim: Option B yield of 3.8 L/m2/day matches tilted wick stills in the literature
law: Sharon et al., tilted wick and basin still, 4.54 and 4.99 L/m2/day (cited in Agrawal and Rana 2019)

claim: Option B wick survives dry stagnation (about 141 C) only with a 150 C fabric
law: Absorbed flux = (U top 6.5 + U back 0.9) x rise, single glazing

claim: Condensate runs down the underside of a 20 deg glass cover to the low-edge gutter as a film
law: Clean glass is wetted by water (low contact angle), so film-wise condensation drains along the slope; standard in tilted stills
check: 20 deg is above the 10 to 15 deg usually needed for drops to run on clean glass
